utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. And good afternoon, General. Could I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, it still applies. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, yesterday you mentioned that you and Goran Mitevski and Minister Boskoski used to meet and you made all possible efforts to make an on-site investigation in Ljuboten village. This is at page 3586 of the transcript. Were these meetings or discussions with Mr. Mitevski, Mr. Boskoski and yourself, was that before the commission that you were a member of issued its report on the 4th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer precisely because we would be in session or we would meet on a daily basis literally. Sometimes even several times in a day and this is why I can't remember when exactly what you mentioned took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Before the commission issued its report on the 4th of September, did Minister Boskoski ever make any comments that you heard about the work that the commission was doing?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed this issue several times, and I know that everyone, using his own line of contacts and command, would seek support from the international community. I don't know what the minister did and whom he discussed the issues with. I know that I discussed with the General, I don't know if I remember his name correctly. Maybe it was Spanner, head of the NATO unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, I'm sorry, but you're not answering the question that I asked you. My question was simply this: Before the committee produced its final report, did Minister Boskoski make any comments in your presence about the work that the commission was doing?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I answered in the affirmative that we discussed the issues several times with --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what comments, if you can recall, did Minister Boskoski make?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't quote but it was along the lines that it should be investigated what took place there. And I know that in one of the meetings even the public prosecutor general was present. Because we made serious efforts to enter the village and to make the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. General, after the commission produced its report on the 4th of September, 2001, did you ever hear Minister Boskoski make any comments about the report?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you recall whether Minister Boskoski asked you and the other members to do anymore work on the report?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer precisely. I know that the director Mitevski relayed some information from the minister to me several times. I tried yesterday and I would like to clarify now, if you allow me, I would like to shed more light on the situation in which the committee worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think I'd like to you answer my question, please. So your answer to my question whether Minister Boskoski asked you and the other members to do more work is you're not sure, you couldn't answer?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him telling me directly, but I know that the Director Mitevski relayed a message from the minister several times, but the minister instructed him or gave him guidelines, I'm not sure. I couldn't quote exactly what was the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that after the report was produced or before?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that such comments or discussions took place both before and after the -- afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters ask that the microphone be moved closer to the witness? We can't hear him clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you move closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What would also help, General, is if you lifted your voice as though you were speaking to Mr. Saxon. Your voice is extremely quiet, and that means that it is not being picked up even though the microphones are close to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Help us, please. What were the instructions or guidelines that Minister Boskoski relayed to Director Mitevski, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I also answered this. First I apologise for the voice I was using. This is the best I can do. I will try to speak up a bit. I couldn't answer precisely, but I will repeat again. I remember well on several occasions the Director Mitevski told me that the minister insisted that the decisions are followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move to a slightly different topic, General, if I may. I'd like to ask you to turn your mind back to Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001, the day the events in Ljuboten village occurred. Do you recall on that afternoon, the afternoon of the 12th, do you recall that you ordered a police unit to go to the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time in the day, but my subordinate, Goran Goergievski, who was in charge of the <<posebna>> units, was given an order by me over the telephone, because I was rather far from Skopje at that time to the scene with the personnel that he had available at that time from his unit in order to prevent direct clash between the civilian population from the village of Ljuboten and from the neighbouring villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, before you --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, I apologise, my learned colleague, but again in line 19, the word – page 4, line 19, the word "posebna" was interpreted as "special."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Galevski, before you issued this order to Goran Georgievski to bring his unit to the area of Ljuboten, did you consult with anyone, or did you just decide to issue the order?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that on that day there were several occasions that I spoke on the phone with both the minister and the Director Goran Mitevski with, my subordinate in charge of the uniformed part of the police force, Skopje, Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski, the colleague that I've mentioned Goran Georgievski, and there must have been other colleagues whose names I could not recall at the moment, or enumerate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So I think is the answer to my question, then, you might have consulted with your colleagues in the Ministry of the Interior before issuing the order to Goran Georgievski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I could have, but I probably have had consulted with him, because it was related to the Skopje region, I must have spoken to Ljupco Bliznakovski, who was in charge of the uniformed police in the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would you have consulted with anyone else outside of the circle of persons that you have referred to?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday, General, you -- you explained how police officers and police inspectors interviewed suspects of crimes at police stations and how then reports and Official Notes were produced based on the information received. Do you remember explaining that to us yesterday? Just yes or no, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is at pages 3597 to 3598 of the transcript. General, if you could take a look at tab 15 in your binder. Tab 15 contains 65 ter 430.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And while the usher is there could we please ask him to turn on the right-hand side microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, we can see that the right-hand microphone is turned off. Could you turn that on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, if we could start with the first page in the Macedonian version, which bears ERN N005-1061. And we have a translation in English as well. You see, General, this is a document from the city secretariat of the interior, administration of operative matters, division of serious crimes. Do you see that at the upper left?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then we see bearer Aleksovski Bobi and then date below that, 26th January, 1989, Skopje and there's a stamp further down to the right. It says evidence. There's a number and a year that's difficult to read in the Macedonian version. Up at the top middle it says operative information and then a bit lower down we see it says subject, threat to security. Are with you me, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The first paragraph begins: "On the 5th of December, 1988" --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object to the relevance of the document because we don't see what makes this document relevant, document of 26th of January, 1989 in relation to the events in 2001. Secondly, my learned colleague should tell us whether it is was ascertained that those people are related to some Ljuboten events, are they related or otherwise to some crimes that the Prosecutor claims were committed, and whether these deeds were known to the witness in any possible way. Otherwise, we see no relevance for a document dated 1989 being shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I rely too precisely, I would simply like to indicate that if you review pages 864 to 870 of the transcript of this trial, you will see a person named on this document mentioned in the transcript. And that is essentially the relevance as to why I want to bring this document to the Chamber's attention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, the first paragraph talks about a person named Kuzmanov Zoran who was attacked without reason by unknown persons. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then in section III, there's a Roman numeral III, says, "We're going to undertake measures to uncover the names of the HH persons," and then there's a sentence, it says,"There is a justified suspicion that the probably wrongdoers are the brothers Janevski Vlado and Aleksander. Are you following with me?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And below that it says persons Janevski Vlado "Kunta," father, Pero, mother Ljiljana. I have a question for you General. In the Macedonian language is the name Pero sometimes a short version of the name Petar?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are two different names with a common source. You can find many people with the name Pero and their ID card also bears that name, Pero.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But would someone named Petar sometimes be referred to as Pero?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It could be a pet name for Petar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see a man Vlado Janevski, Kunta, born on the 8th of September, 1965 in Skopje, who they live on the street City Park number 13. Below that we see Vlado's brother Janevski Aleksander, same parents, born on the 8th of July, 1969, living at the same address. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now back -- and then we see the drafter is Aleksovski Bobi. Now, back in the late 1980s would such operative information have been recorded in this way?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, you will see the nickname Kunta at paragraph 870 of the transcript, and Kunta was referred to as a member of the security forces that were with Johan Tarculovski in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001, and this gentleman known as Kunta suffered a wound at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to what is page 2, please. Turn to the next page, General. This is a document -- it is also operative information from the city secretariat of the interior, administration of the operative matters, division of serious crimes. Same bearer, Aleksovski Bobi is a typist mentioned. This is about a year earlier than -- actually, no, it is drafted around the same time. It is from December, 1988. Again the subject, threat to security and we have the same victim, Zoran Kuzmanov can you see man off who is reporting in the first paragraphs that on two occasions he was attacked by unknown persons who had previously threatened to kill him. Did you see that, General? First paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph we see the names Janevski Aleksander and Janevski Vlado mentioned again. It says there was an interview with Vlado and then there's a sentence about apparently Vlado being in a drunken state and then we see again persons Janevski Vlado, Kunta, father Pero, mother Ljiljana, born on the 8th of September, 1965, in Skopje. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So would this also have been a typical way that operative information was recorded in the late 1980s?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the usual way in which it is done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender these two documents, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For what purpose, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like the Chamber to know the true name of the man known as Kunta and I would like to know something about -- I would like the Chamber to know something about the background of the man known as Kunta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The material so far is relevant to those is already on the transcript, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. All we have on the transcript -- I'm sorry, I did not explain myself clearly. On page 870, we have a nickname, Kunta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But we do not have the true name of the person known as Kunta, because the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But the transcript now has connected a person with the nickname Kunta with the named person on these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is revealed in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But I would also like the Chamber to have evidence related to the criminal background of persons who were in the village with Johan Tarculovski on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will not receive the documents, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to tab 11. This is 65 ter number 657. General, this is a document, it is a decision, actually, issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs on the 29th of May, 2001 in Skopje. It is a decision to form the headquarters of the operative action Ramno. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you see on the bottom, you see there's a signature of Ljube Boskoski, the minister for the internal affairs. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that on the first page, if you look at number 3, we see your name, Risto Galevski, as a person who will be part of this headquarters. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the headquarters of operative action Ramno? What work did it do?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision itself, item 1 of it reads: "In order to organise head, coordinate, and direct the measures and activities related to the operational action Ramno, the headquarters is established."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tell us please again what was operative action Ramno then?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operational action Ramno was the name for the overall activities related to the resolving of the problems that happened at the very beginning of 2001 in the village of Tanusevci and continuously spread towards the neighbouring villages in the Kumanovo Skopje and Tetovo regions. All of these activities were managed by these same and it was the operational action named Ramno.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P381, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed, Ms. Residovic, we were just letting you have time to get things collected together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. And in order to avoid interrupting the witness later, we have quite a number of documents, Your Honours, that we wish to show this witness in the course of cross-examination, so I would like to ask for the assistance of the usher in distributing these documents, and they are compiled in three binders, to the Chamber, to the witness, and to the colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Galevski.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux we appear for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I start asking you questions that I have planned for you, I will kindly ask you to listen to a warning that I wish to issue to you. You and I speak languages that we could understand, that the languages are not the same but we are able to understand one another and you could answer the question that I'm asking very rapidly, but I kindly ask to you wait for my question to be interpreted so that the Court and the colleagues in the courtroom are able to know what is it that I'm asking and then what is your answer to my question. Have you understood this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1975 you finished your police high school and you started working at the police right away. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said to my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, in the course of your work you also graduated from the security faculty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until 1992 you used to work in the traffic police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you were on the duty of a deputy and later on you were a commander of the Kisela Voda police station in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy commander in the traffic police station and after that I was assigned a commander in the other stations. I was not a deputy, I was directly a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, you were appointed a head -- a chief inspector in the public order and security department with the purpose to improve the methodology of the police work and you were later appointed a head of the administration of public law and order. Are these information correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2000, you were appointed deputy of the under-secretary in the Ministry of Interior for the police, and on the 11th of April, 2001, you were appointed under-secretary in the Ministry of Interior for the police; is that true?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During your -- when you were appointed as an under-secretary for the police, Dosta Dimovska was the minister of interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the police academy was established and after it was in full swing as a personal request that you filed to the government, the government of the Republic of Macedonia appointed you on 12th of February, 2002 director of the police academy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes. At that time it was called a centre for education for personnel of the security fields and since that was an institution that was about to be discontinued, this was supposed to be transported in the police academy which took place in -- sometime in mid-2003 as a police academy and that has been functioning continually since then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you are -- you now bear the rank of a police general. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since sometime in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have already testified in August 2001, you were at the position of the under-secretary for the police within the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I were to say that you -- in 2001, you were the -- the chief of all uniformed police expect for -- until August 2001 the Tigers unit then that statement would be correct. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until August 2001, the special Tiger unit was linked to the minister of the interior. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that in addition to the education you got in the Republic of Macedonia, you underwent a number of specialist courses abroad, where you acquired additional knowledge from the police practice and operations area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind all these duties that you were carrying out, I would ask you to answer several questions of mine that are linked to the competencies, the organisation of work of the ministry, especially about the position, the rights and obligations of the minister, to the extent that you are aware of. You remember that my learned colleague asked you yesterday about the establishment of the commission or one of the commissions that were established on 13th of August that you were a member of and the other commission that was established by Minister Boskoski. The first one was established by Minister Boskoski, and the second one that was later established by Minister Hari Kosta. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the first one and I don't remember the second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you remember that you were asked by my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, yesterday about it?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the question of the commission -- of the commission, its work and operation might be important for the manner of work within the Ministry of Interior, I'll be free to ask you several questions on these matters as well. Before I go on to some specific questions from this area, I would like to ask you whether my statement would be correct, that during your entire work in the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, so also in 2001, you and all the members of the ministry were obliged to act according to the domestic legislation according to the laws and regulations that were adopted based on that law?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The application of the regulations, the procedures prescribed by law and the competences of the bodies that were envisioned with the laws of the Republic of Macedonia were also applicable in 2001, meaning in the time of the crisis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that in the Ministry of the Interior there was also a principle that information coming from the lower organisational units of the Ministry, that is to say organs which are on a lower level of hierarchy, should be trusted?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the ministry of any country, but we could not speak of those because those facts are not even known to me, but surely for the ministry of the Republic of Macedonia, the ministry has been basing its information, plans, and programmes on the law and the trust in the information that it would acquire from its own structure, from its bodies, units that within the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the system that has been operational for years.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, General, tell me, since we already are speaking about the laws that regulated the organisation, the operation and the competency, is it true that the law on organisation work of the bodies of certain administration was the one that prescribed the basic principle of organisation, the competency, and the operation of all the state administration bodies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such a law exists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The ministries in line with the laws of the Republic of Macedonia are part of the state administration, so this law also applied to some general competencies of the ministries so thus also of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, for the Ministry of Interior there was a special law that is the law on the Ministry of Interior, that set the -- the competency, the scope, the organisation of the ministry and also other issues that are important for its operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if there are certain evidences already spoken before this Court, but I would like to ask you, General, is that correct that the framework of competencies of the interior in line with the law were the affairs of the public and the state security. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like you to repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct that the Ministry of Interior covered the scope of the public security as well as it was in charge of the state security?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I'm sorry for asking you. I can hear you, I understand your question, I understand your language, but then I'm also hearing in Macedonian and that confuses me a little bit, but the answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Keeping these competences in mind of the public and state security, is that correct, General, that within the Ministry of Interior there were two main parts organised, the first one being the bureau for public security which encompassed all the affairs of public security as well as the administration for security and counter-intelligence that was in charge of the affairs of state security. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And each of these parts was -- of the ministry was headed by a minister. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, director, not minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Administration for state security was acting in -- in summary that was the uniformed police that was primarily in charge to maintain the law and order and it also consisted of a criminal police that -- whose primary task was to prevent the commitment of crimes and detection and prosecution of perpetrators in the pre-criminal procedure -- in the pre-trial procedure. Is that the basic task of these parts within the public security?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your department of the police was in the public security sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your immediate superior was the director of the public security bureau; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, as you already said to my learned colleague, Goran Mitevski was at that position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 2001 it was Zvonko Kasirski, and I don't remember exactly when it started, but then it was Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In August 2001, Goran Mitevski was the one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In August it was already Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you now to look in your binder number 1 in tab 1/1, so small 1. To look the Exhibit P92, number N001-9490, and the English version is the same number with the addition of ET, so 9409-ET. So, General, is this the law on the organisation and the operation of the state administration bodies of which you testified a while ago that is in charge of certain general questions of the operation of all of the ministries as well as the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to turn to page 2 of this document. There is N001-9504. And English version is the same with the addition of ET. And you can see there that in Article 47 of this law -- I apologise. That is N001-9504. That is the second page in this binder but not of the law. So it refers to Article 47. So N001-9504. And while we're waiting to see this text displayed on the screen -- I apologise. I might have misspoken. 9490 is the English version, and 009504 would be the document in the Macedonian version. In any event, that is Article 47. So I would like to go back a page backwards. All right. Thank you. Article 47 lists what is applicable to all the ministries in general, that is, that the ministries are headed by a minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 49 lists that the minister represents the ministry. It organises it and ensures enforcement of the laws and the -- works in line and that it adopts other acts and also adopts other measures that under its competencies and that are in line with the law. Is that a general position for the ministries as well as the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is applicable to all the ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask now to look into page N009525 [as interpreted], the Macedonian version, Article 55, and English version is N001-949 -- I can't really read what is written there. Okay. The Article is 55. I apologise. I'm not able to see exactly in this range what is the number of that page. But what I want to ask you is that what is envisioned by Article 55 and that is whether it is under the competence of all the ministries, as well as the Ministry of Interior, to adopt rules, orders, directives, plans, and other decisions based on which the employees of a certain ministry would carry out the laws and the other regulations. Is it what was the competence also of the Ministry of Interior, whereby you worked?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to -- I would like to ask you something now. Is it true that the position of the minister of the interior was actually -- had the general competences to represent the ministry to adopt regulations and general programmes, plans of work, the minister was not the operational body that was managing the units and the bodies within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like -- I would answer like this. The minister was and is a manager of the ministry but while the operative affairs are carried out by operative workers. He carries no work on the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look into this document that is found under this large tab 1 numbered 2, and that is Exhibit P86 and I would like to ask -- I will ask that the Macedonian page is turned N000-8983. So that is Articles 8 and 9 that are of our interest, while the English page should also be N000-8964. This -- General, we can see here the scope of work and the organisation of the ministry. The subheading is police. General, is that the part -- that part of the police that was in your department, that is, the department headed by you in 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. This article covers my work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, General, that Article 8 actually confirms your answer that you gave about the substance and the basic tasks carried out by the uniformed part of the Ministry of Interior, that is to say, the police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 9 reads that: "For the immediate execution of the police and other interior activities, at least one police station is established in each of the municipalities." Do you see that written?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you, General, is it true that when I say that the basic works of the police listed in Article 8 are carried out in the basic police units. That is to say, in the police stations or the basic police bodies, that is the departments within the municipalities, or sectors in the cities?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you, as a head of the entire department of the police in the Republic of Macedonia, were not in a position also to immediately manage to -- that is to carry out the police works in the field directly. That was the task of the authorised officials in the basic units of the ministry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, General, that in the essence, the operations of the Ministry of Interior were -- are mainly carried out by the authorised officials, that is, persons who are authorised that are originating directly from the law?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a police officer for the majority of the tasks carried out needs no order but the police officer, bearing in mind his position, carries out its works pursuant to the law?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But it is also correct that the police might act upon orders as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And mainly in live -- in the majority of the cases a police officer or an authorised official in the criminal police receives the order from his or her immediate superior, that is to say, the commander of the police station or the head of the department of the interior within the municipality. Is that the way how things work in the police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the commander most often who directly does this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the immediate managers, the immediate superiors, actually are issuing daily orders related to the legal execution of the police work, and, if necessary, they also issue specific orders for work of each of the police officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the law, an authorised official, in addition to the uniformed police and persons employed in the criminal police, are also persons higher in the commanding rank, so you were also an authorised official. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the law, the minister was also an authorised official; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the rule-book for organisation of the work of the Ministry of Interior establishes the scope of operation of each of the authorised officials, so it was neither under your competence nor under the competence of the minister was to operatively carry out the tasks nor to effectively control the police officers in the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The director of public security and the director of state security as well as the state secretary in the interior ministry, all of -- none of them were appointed by the interior minister. They were appointed directly by the government. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the government appointed them upon the proposal of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask to you look at this document which is in tab 4. This is an excerpt from the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, number 40, from 2001. It is 65 ter 1D462. This is one page. It's 1D4261. In the Macedonian text, under number 819, you can see that a decision was adopted for the appointment of the director of public security. You already told me that in -- somewhere in 2001 Goran Mitevski became director of the public security bureau. In this text, we can see that on May 15th, 2001 the government of the Republic of Macedonia had appointed as director of the public security bureau Goran Mitevski who was, until then, charge -- director of the security and counter-intelligence division. Does this document confirm your testimony that it is the government which appoints the director of the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the government, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 1D4262 of the English version, there is also a text of the previous page of this Official Gazette, and here we can see under item 815 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, there is 1D462 [as interpreted]. I was informed that this page is not in your binder, but I will read this part. It says: [In English] "The government of the Republic of Macedonia of the session held on 15 May 2001, submit a resolution for the appointment of the director of the security and counterintelligence division. [Interpretation] And under [In English] Point 1 is "Dr. Zoran Verusevski, associate professor for the security faculty in Skopje, is appointed as a director of the security and counter-intelligence division organ of the structure in the Ministry of Interior." [Interpretation] Therefore, from this, we can conclude that at the same meeting the government appointed also the director of the state security bureau. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I seek to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D105, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But the fact that the director of the state security bureau is appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia, is it correct that it is the assembly which conducts the control over the work of the state security pursuant to the law?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a parliamentary committee in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at the document in tab 5. This is 65 ter 1D207. It's is only one page, Your Honour. We have only a draft translation of the document. When the final translation is ready, we will also submit it. General, you have before you an excerpt from the web site of the interior ministry which establishes the competences of the director of the public security bureau and institution itself. I will read it and I will ask you to tell me whether this is the accurate position of the director of the public security bureau. It says: "The public security bureau, it is headed by the director who upon the proposal of a minister is appointed or dismissed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia for a mandate of four years. The director is independent in conducting his duties within the bureau and he responds for -- he's held responsible for his work before the minister and before the government upon the proposal of the director of the bureau the minister adopts acts for the administration and the work and the systemization of the jobs within the bureau and this undergoes an approval from the government. Are this information accurate in relation to the position of the director of the bureau?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would like to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes that before we can be sure of the probative value of this document and relevance, it needs to be established whether the text as it is expressed here or the principles that were -- are expressed here were also in force in the summer of 2001, because it's my understanding that this was taken from the web site of the Ministry of Interior on the 18th of April in 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we said that we took it from the web site. I just wanted to show it to the witness who was at a high ranking position within the Ministry of Interior and to ask him to confirm whether this competence was accurate. If the witness can confirm it, then we propose this document to be accepted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point is when was it operative and whether it was operative at the time relevant to the indictment. Can you assist with us with respect to that, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This could explain the witness. I will ask the witness about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, General, whether this -- whether the director of the public security has this -- had this position in 2001, whether there was such a position in 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was such a position as in 1999 when this position was in fact established.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this answer is sufficient, then I would seek to tender this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes the question should be whether the information about the public safety bureau as expressed in this printout from the web site also was in force or also was applicable to the public safety bureau and its director in the summer of 2001. And I don't think the last question and answer give us that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think there is need for something more from the witness, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you heard the directives of the Honourable Bench to my question. You answered that this was a competence even before 2001. But the competence could have stopped before 2001 and my precise question would be whether this was a competence of the director of the public security bureau also in 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the document in tab 10. Respectively before this Court, the witness M-37 testified, who -- to a question: "[In English] Is it correct that M-37 that in actual fact the task and responsibility of the police were set out in the -- in the law, primarily the law of the interior and in the field of crime in the law of criminal procedure of the Republic of Macedonia? Is that right?" "Yes, that is right." [Interpretation] Do you also agree, General, that the tasks of police officers were primarily prescribed by law, as the witness testified?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago we spoke about the way the law regulates the basic competences and basic organisation of the interior ministry. Is it correct, Mr. General, that the internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior affairs, its organisational scope, the administration and the responsibility for conducting -- for executing the duties are defined by the rule for organisation and work of the interior ministry?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the document in tab 6. This is it exhibit 1D64. This was only marked for identification, and, Your Honour, at the moment, when we showed this document to an earlier witness, we gave the translation of only few articles. Now we have prepared the whole text of the document, both in Macedonian and in English, and after the questioning of this witness, we will seek to tender this as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you see, -- you're looking at the first page of the rule for the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior from January 2001. Is this the rule regulating the issues that I asked you before?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at the last page of this document. This is 1D4389, and the English version is 1D4413. The document is accompanied also by a chart. I have showed only the last page. Therefore, 1D4389, and the English version is 1D4413. You can see that this rule was adopted on January 26th, 2001, when Dosta Dimovska was minister of the interior. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 1D4372, Macedonian version, and 1D4393, English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There would be a confusion on the e-court. I have been warned that the whole text was -- was under number 65 ter 217.1 and the pages were as I have read them before, 1D4372 Macedonian version and 1D4393.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we are waiting for the document to appear on the screen, we all have the hard copy before us. You have already found the first page of documents. Did you find the first page, General? Could you please look at Article 2. It says that the work of the ministry is headed by the minister of the interior, is this the general competence related to the heading of the ministry, which is in accordance what we have seen concerning the overall state bodies?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The last Article says that the bureau of public security as an organ within the ministry is headed by the director. Is this what you said before, that the director is a person heading the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. It is probably completely my fault but I am simply lost. I'm not sure where my colleague is reading from, and I don't see that she's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We haven't got it on the screen because the number given is not correct. The court officer is trying to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The number you've given starts at an article later than the one you want referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I could make questions -- no, I apologise. It would be better to have the document, but it is obvious that at this moment we cannot speak of these rule-book, and I will turn to something else until we find the correct pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would it be easier for you to have the break now? We're within three minutes of the break time. And enable the document to be found during the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You have solved the problem. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will do that and resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I would like now that the witness is shown 65 ter 217.1. That is page 1D4372, and the English version, page 1D4393. This -- it is under tab 6 in this binder. That is the first page --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, found in tab 6. That is the rule-book for organisation and operation of the Ministry of Interior. Please turn the page and you'll see the page we are looking for with the number 1D4372. Did you find it? It starts with Article 1.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The preamble of this rule-book reads that the rule-book is adopted based on Article 55, paragraph 1, of the law on organisation and work of the bodies of the state administration. Do you remember, General, that when we were looking at this law we saw that it is under the competence of any ministry as well as the Ministry of Interior to adopt rule-books and other by-laws. Is that what we already saw in the mentioned law?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 2 -- you can see in Article 2 that the minister heads the work of the Ministry of Interior, that is, also if we recall the law on the organisation of the state administration, that is a general provision that establishes that all the -- all the ministers as well as the Ministry of Interior heads the ministry as an administrative body. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph of Article 2, it is stipulated that the public security bureau as a body under the ministry is headed by a director, and this is the position of the director of public security that you previously described. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 3 of this rule-book reads: "For the execution of the work under the competence of the public security bureau two departments are established, police department and criminal police department, and a number of independent organisational forms." The rule-book with this provision actually sets forth what you testified about, about the way the public security bureau is organised; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to turn to page 8 of this rule-book, that is Article 8. And the Macedonian version is 1D4379, and the English version is page number 1D4401. This article, General, you can see that for the conduction of the internal affairs of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, following regional organisational forms of the ministry are established. And then there are 11 sectors listed, sectors of the interior, on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, General, is this article reading that the execution of the internal affairs the sectors as established, does this confirm what you already said, that the basic affairs of the Ministry of Interior are carried out actually in the basic forms of operation of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it confirms it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look into Article 21. That is on page 16 of this rule-book that. Is the Macedonian page 1D4387, and English page is 1D4410. And, General, I would like to ask you to look into this article and to see whether that is the article that regulates the competences and the responsibilities of the individual persons within the ministry. The first paragraph of this article reads that: "The different forms in the ministry and the public of the -- in the public safety bureau as a body within the ministry, are headed -- are headed by heads whose title and position are set forth by the book of rules of the systemization of the jobs within the Ministry of Interior, depending on the type of the organisational type. The heads of the department for police and the department for the crime police and the heads of the analysis and investigation sector, the anti-terrorism sector, the helicopter unit, the surveillance and archiving department, the sector for personal protection, the sector for alias and immigration affairs, the sector for fire protection, explosives and danger substances, and the department for the defensive preparations are functionally connected with the head of the public safety bureau and are responsible immediately before the head for the works and the tasks of their area. Do you agree, General, that these -- that hereby those parts of the Ministry of Interior are set forth that are directly responsible to the director for public security. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next article reads: "The commander of the special task unit, the Tiger, and the heads of the internal control department, the international cooperation department and European integration department, the operative techniques sector, the finance sector and other joint works, the sector for legal and the personal affairs, the telecommunications sector, the encrypto protection and the IT and the sector for administrative, supervisory works are connected by their works also with the head of the public security bureau and the head of the safety and counter-intelligence department." Would it be true if I were to say that only these parts of the ministry as well as the special unit the Tigers were directly linked to the minister and responsible before him in accordance to this rule-book from 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I would also add that the special task units because of its features in specific cities was directly linked to the minister, but in the practice the minister never commanded or headed that unit. He only transferred his authority and most frequently that was to the head of the police department. So this is where the approval for use of this unit was given.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, please look into Article 22 now. It reads that the heads of the organisational forms within other organisational form are directly responsible before the head of the appropriate organisational form. The employees are responsible before their immediate heads and the head of the organisational form to which they belong, for the specific execution of their tasks an operations. General, does this article set forth the responsibility of the employees towards the -- their direct superiors?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does regulate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look into Article 26 of this rule-book. Article 26 reads: "A collegium exists within the ministry acting as an advisory body to the minister. The immediate composition of the collegium is composed of the minister, the deputy minister, the director of the public security bureau, the director of the administration for security and counter-intelligence, the heads of the police department and the heads of the criminal police and the state secretary." Tell me, General, is it true that minister head this collegium and that you were also a member of that minister's collegium?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were meetings of the collegium held frequently or less frequently where I participated and I think this was -- he was one of the rare ministers, unlike the others before him or after him, who used to call the meetings of this collegium.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the question of my learned colleague the Prosecutor you answered that on several occasions you used to meet with the Director Mitevski as well as with the minister and that he insisted to investigate or to further investigate the things related to Ljuboten. Would you be able to tell me whether these requests of the minister were primarily expressed at the meetings of the collegium or were there specific meetings called for these matters?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you precisely how many meetings these things were discussed but at one of the meetings where the public prosecutor was present, this topic was discussed and then all the information and the activities that I head or was I supposed to carry out were -- then the order went to the Director Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Article 27 reads that for reviewing of the matters related to the operation of the police department, the criminal police department, and about the other affairs carried out in the organisational forms which are directly functionally related to the director of the public security bureau there is a special experts collegium of the director of the public security bureau. So it could be seen from here that also the director of the public security bureau had his own collegium in which you were also a -- a member. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor in relation to the operation of the -- to the work of the commission asked you whether you had some special meetings. Tell me, please, you responded that you used to meet frequently with the minister, sometimes two or three times a week. Please tell me was this collegium of directors of yours at that time operational and did you meet regularly for the regular affairs and did you meet one or several times in the course of the day?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that we used to meet very often, sometimes one, two, three times a day, and in addition to the activity that came as a result of the investigation of the Ljuboten affairs, we had a number of events that were burdensome for the security of the country. I would primarily mention here the start of the blockade of the regional roads towards the Blace border crossing. That blockade was ongoing for about three weeks or something in the month of August. Another activity that required our attention was the plan to return the police patrols in the crisis areas. That was a period that -- that required literally engagement without any days of rest for all of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, if I understood you well, because of these affairs as well as because of the needs of the work of the collegium you used to meet very often with the director of the public security bureau, Mr. Goran Mitevski. Don't -- do you think that I am right to understand there was no need for some special meetings of the committee consisting of three persons which, according to the book of regulations and because of some other affairs, are meeting regularly and, as you said, you discussed very often during these meetings about the work of the commission that was established by the minister?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. At this period it would have been impossible to meet only because of this, because we had many other events and affairs that we were meeting about. There were a lot of protests, there was a lot of blockades. I mentioned the plan to return the police patrols to the crisis areas, et cetera, so the headquarters or the team of the director or the collegium, the experts collegium, was a -- a -- permanently in operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I would like to ask you the following page that is 1D4839 and Article 28, while the English page is 1D4412. This article that is part of the final for provisions of the book of regulations reads that this rule-book is accompanied by an organisational structure schematic, and is it -- is it customary when changes are made to this book of regulation to also make a schematic representation of all the links existing within the ministry and all the direct lines of responsibility of the bodies towards each other. Is that the usual fashion how these books of regulations were created?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a usual thing to create such an organigram. This is also taking place now in the reforms which actually were initiated during Mr. Boskoski's tenure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us look to the following page which actually is the schematic representation of the relations within the ministry. That is 1D4390 of the Macedonian version and the English version is page number 1D4414. Please have a look at the schematic, and to tell me whether this schematic, this chart, represents the internal links and mutual responsibilities within the ministry as set forth by the book of regulation from January 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This chart exactly represents the rule-book that we previously discussed about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look into this chart, outside of this bold black line of this rectangle that represents the public security bureau, we can see these parts of the ministry that were directly linked to the minister and, among them, only the special Tiger unit from within the ranks of the Special Unit is represented there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Within the Public Security Bureau, you would agree with me that together with the police department headed by you, directly operationally connected to them were the Security Sector which also included sections for the security of the president and the prime minister, security of important facilities and persons, diplomatic and consular sections, and other sections of the Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one speaks about the parts that refer to the providing personal security of the prime minister, the parliament or the president, would you agree with me that de jure -- even though de jure, they were within the public security bureau, the effective control and the -- the effective -- the active control were in the hands of the persons that they were securing, for example, the president of the parliament the president of the republic or --

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, de facto they were under their control. I know this from practical experience.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to jointly look into the document found in tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I go to the next document, I would propose to -- to have the previous text of the exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that was marked for identification to be replaced with this text and to receive the final number 1D64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In what way do the texts differ?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the last time for the purposes for investigation of one of the -- examination of one of the witnesses we only took the provisions of Articles 21 and 22 about the competences of the minister in the organisational chart that was reviewed at that time. We were not able to submit the entire text and its translations, so at that time I said that it might be good to mark the document for identification until we are able to provide the entire text of the rule-book to the Court, and its translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive the whole document as a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 1D107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to ask you now to look into the document found in tab 7, that is exhibit number 1D65. The page is 2D437, the Macedonian version, and 1D2403 is the English version page. General, this is the rule-book amending the rule-book on organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior of June 2001, and my question to you is whether it is correct that all amendments to the rule-book were adopted also through an act issued by the minister as rule-books amending the previous -- the original rule-books?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a rule-book is amending with an act containing the amendments and additions to the rule-book?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. This is the right of the minister; it is probably proposed by one of his associates.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you now look at 1D2348, Macedonian. 1D2404, Article 2 tells us that a new sector for operative reconnaissance is introduced. And in page 1D2349, and the English page 1D2405, we have a new chart which adds to the earlier chart also this new sector established through the rule-book amending the rule-book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this rule-book, there are no changes of the -- to the competences of the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated earlier, General, that the minister transferred certain competences to you as the under-secretary for police, also in relation to the Special Unit Tiger, actually the competences to use that unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. He is authorised to put the unit into use and he places the unit under the command of the head of police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, to look at the document in tab 8. That is the Exhibit 1D66. Macedonian page is 1D2321, while the English page is 1D2407. This is, you would agree with me, General, yet another amendment to the rule-book on the organisation an operation of the Ministry of Interior adopted in August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you turn to the following page, 1D2322 Macedonian, and 1D2408 English, the Article 1, after enumerating these various amendments to the rule-book, in the second-before-the-last paragraph reads: "From the 1st of August, 2001, the item 1, special tasks unit Tiger from the Article 7 is moved to the part A, department for police, in Article 4 and becomes item 6." And the Article 3 reads that in the Article 21, if you remember those were the competences of the minister, in the items 3 and 4, the words "the commander of the special tasks unit Tigers and" are erased. Is it correct that this rule-book confirms the earlier decision of the minister that actually transfers the competences to use the Tigers unit to the head for police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the -- in the organisational sense, yes. The order, or the authorisation to use this unit remain with the minister. So organisation-wise, it belongs now to the police department since August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look now at the chart behind this page, 1D2323, 1D2409. Does this chart now, General, represent the change of status, actually the position, of the unit for special tasks Tiger, in the way established by the rule-book?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it represents that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have looked at the rule-book on organisation operation of the public security. Is it also correct, General, that there is a rule-book on the organisation and operation of the security and counter-intelligence department?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen it, but I believe it happens -- it exists and it would be logical for it to exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the business conducted by this part of the Ministry of the Interior, you could agree with me if I say that their ways of operation, the methods of operation are slightly different than those used by the public security?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is why they're not titled public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I can understand that your answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The work of the public security using its own structures then the links in the enemy's forces, links to foreigners, then use of operational means, et cetera, provides an opportunity for the state security to gather significant information of importance for the security of the country. Is this conclusion of mine correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. This is why they exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that the information so gathered and the knowledge verified by state security are attached importance and confidence in the course of assessment of certain situations, especially when issues of security of the state are at stake?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we speak about those competences of the minister to pass certain general acts could you agree with me, General, that it is true the adoption of a general act that the minister is running the ministry and not by issuing specific tasks to authorised officers. So, his way of management is primarily through the establishment of procedures, adoption of rule-books, instructions, guidelines or any other general acts?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, your conclusion is correct. Through the instruments available to him, he takes care about the legality in the operation and enforcement of the laws and secondary legislation in force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when a minister issues a guideline or adopts a rule-book, then the authorised officers in that area have the duty to act upon that rule-book and they do not need any special orders issued for any specific case and the instructions how they should proceed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at this document in tab 12. That is Exhibit P94 and the number, Macedonian is R042-4710, while the English is R042-471DT, this is draft, which means draft translation of the document, because the original translation is still not received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, this is Prosecutor's draft translation. It is it obvious that it was not translated. But we had no objections, as you know, Your Honours. Not all documents need to be translated again by the ICTY because we did not believe there were problems here with the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
